title: Archival xenon exposures reinterpreted for the extended window: what LUX, XENON1T, PandaX-II and LZ's own first run already said
question: How many high-energy events should LZ SR1 (0.90 t yr), XENON1T (1.0), LUX 2021 (0.09) and PandaX-II 2019 (0.15 t yr) have contained under LZ's best fit given their ROI edges; are the digitised Fig. 6 previous limits consistent with those counts; what does a joint Poisson likelihood LZ(1)+archival(0) do to the rate, interval and significance; and what would a joint SR1+SR3 fit give?
headline_result: The archival exposures owed 0.29-0.34 events at LZ's best fit, 0.29-0.32 of them in LZ's own SR1 (P(0)=0.73), <=0.03 elsewhere because their windows end below the signal; adding their zeros lowers the fitted rate by 22-25% and the local Z by 0.07 sigma; the digitised SR1 limits correspond to 2-3 zero-event counts (1.96 at delta=250 keV) and lie 6-30x above the new best fit; the SR1 L10 limits imply 2.6-3.2 events in LZ's normalisation but 0.68-0.83 in the WimPyDD/Anand one, favouring P012's convention
model_or_mechanism: xenon-target universality; WimPyDD O1 inelastic (1000 GeV, Sun-frame Baxter halo) and L10 spectra normalised to 1 LZ event, folded with recalled archival acceptances; Poisson likelihood combination; PyMuPDF digitisation of Fig. 6 previous limits inverted to implied counts / effective exposures
confidence: medium - exposure ratios and Poisson arithmetic exact, normalisations validated (P035 1.000-1.001, P012 0.999), but archival ROIs, SR1 g1 and the SR1 high-energy event count are recalled
agent_tools: Read x15, Bash x24, Write x4, Edit x13, ToolSearch x2, Monitor x1, TaskStop x4
software_and_packages: python 3.12.13; WimPyDD 2.0.4 (eft_hamiltonian, streamed_halo_function, diff_rate via lzcommon); numpy 2.5.3; scipy 1.18.1 (special.erf, optimize.minimize_scalar/brentq); pandas 3.0.5; matplotlib 3.11.2; pymupdf 1.28.2 (get_drawings); common/lzcommon.py
